# Paper identification and audit scope

Title: *You give them something to eat: Dietary Diversity, Coverage, and Catholic Aid in Rwanda*. First genuine referee revision; public default branch codex/research. No journal manuscript ID. Internal self-audit follows the public JPE TEMPLATE.qmd criteria and retained MIT template attribution; not JPE certification or an independent referee replication.

# Data, rights and access

Default inputs are all public and supplied under data/input. No access application or credentials. Original corrected deposit: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15881329, actual CC BY 4.0/open metadata preserved in docs/sources/zenodo-rights.json. Old restricted deposit is excluded. Core household panel has 5,506 rows/52 numeric fields. Supplementary household panel has 5,506 matched rows; child extract 7,356 numeric rows. Names, contacts, geographic/date identifiers, free text and administrative lists are not exported. Arbitrary keys preserve linkage/assignment. Numeric checks supplement field review, not universal anonymity proof.

Source extraction verifies corrected archive MD5 and SHA256, reads exact members and checks independently pinned derived bytes before replacing inputs. Generated provenance cannot silently overwrite the immutable reference. The adversarial audit rejects altered data with a rewritten generated manifest and rejects a corrupt archive. Raw archive excluded from Git. Both source extractors are supplied; no manually extracted file can replace their verified member reads.

Upstream survey cleaning is outside the inputs. Original labels plus analytical-codebook.json document source preprocessing limits, missing replacements, monetary transformations and anthropometric scope. Initial integer diet matches all 5,414 complete source modules. Item-informed revision identifies two additional eligible endline diets; full-population intervals retain every 1,793 baseline eligible household. One-household discrepancy from published baseline count remains disclosed.

# Software, requirements and master

Python 3.12.10 with NumPy 2.5.2, pandas 3.0.5, SciPy 1.18.1 and Matplotlib 3.11.1; requirements-lock.txt pins all tested transitive dependencies. Existing MiKTeX 25.12 provides optional pdflatex; no TeX installation required here. Optional source extraction openpyxl 3.1.5; visual/cold-copy checks PyMuPDF/Pillow; separate optional prose screen dependencies documented. Optional Stata/MP 19 uses built-in commands only. No language model enters scientific estimates.

Windows 11 x64, eight available logical processors. No GPU, API or network after installation. Practical allowance 2 GB RAM/150 MB reproduction space, plus packages. Physical RAM not measured. Complete revised master/PDF takes approximately 38 seconds here; installation additional.

Single command python run.py --pdf verifies input references, invokes initial estimate, referee_revision, finite_cluster, both exhibit builders and both validators, then compiles three times. python run.py omits PDF only. --from-source invokes both direct-ZIP extractors. Random seed 20260930, 9,999 draws. All scripts use project-relative paths.

# Output mapping

docs/output-map.csv derives numbering from the actual manuscript and maps all nineteen tables, four figures and both empirical macro files to builder locations and numerical outputs. Initial tables/macro values come from estimate.py; new coherent distributions, bounds, regret, costs and populations from referee_revision.py; CR2/omissions from finite_cluster.py. Source experiment facts, theory proofs and citations require source/mathematical review; a script exit does not establish them.

The initially repeated nulls are deduplicated: 204 primary tests (221 display rows), 96 secondary (104 rows). Food categories 80, baseline heterogeneity ten, observation five. Revision families 184 GK/cash, 828 pairwise, 1,656 endpoint tests, removing affine repetitions. Child and ineligible outcomes have separate fifteen-test Holm families. New analyses are exploratory after genuine review; dated plan amendments retained.

# Performed checks

Core validation: 33/33 including actual independent Stata agreement for five unchanged mean-ANCOVA effects (coefficient error below 1.3e-13, SE below 5.2e-15). Revision validation: 92/92, including coherent CDF/mean/shortfall identities, cohort partition, interval ordering, known probabilities, 100 independent LP comparisons (max error below 4.5e-15), tamper rejection and numeric child extract keys. CR2 checks its stated working-model sandwich expectation identities. These tests do not prove selection ignorability or exact finite-design interval coverage.

Final cold-output audit used the installed interpreter and passed all 60 estimate/table/macro/PNG/PDF-text comparisons for the current revision. Each audit JSON records actual scope. First-submission published commit 046ce79 separately passed 29 comparisons after a genuinely fresh official-PyPI install. A new frozen-source export will rerun the revised package in that separately installed locked environment; no fresh reinstallation is asserted for the revision. Runtime metadata, PDF timestamps and optional Stata reference excluded from byte checks.

Rendered contact sheets and higher-resolution title/tables were visually reviewed. The overlong compound anthropometric label and a lone bibliography spill page were repaired in source. Final 32-page PDF was rerendered after all edits and inspected; no clipped content or unresolved references remain. Render checks are independent of compilation success.

# Interpretation and classification

HDDS is household food access, not child nutritional adequacy. Coherent ratio inference is village-cluster asymptotic, not exact blocked randomization; CR2 is a defined working-model sensitivity. Full-baseline missing-diet endpoints have sampling bands; initial coarse regions do not. Costs fixed; take-up/cost grids hold effects fixed and are accounting scenarios, not causal forecasts. Transport requires stable package delivery/no cross-village interference. Hard realized caps/activation overhead need further inputs. Model is an illustration, not identified saving mediation.
